summary: Southern California Edison files tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in ER27-508-000, answering the CAISO show cause order. A new Appendix XV sets large load interconnection procedures, with a study deposit, a 15-year minimum revenue obligation backed by security, exit fees and a curtailable interim service. More than 250 pages of tariff sheets follow the letter.
ask: Accept the revisions as filed, effective February 16, 2027, and rescind the show cause order as to SCE's tariff.

points.point: SCE takes CAISO's 50 MW definition into its tariff.
points.quote: SCE proposes to incorporate the CAISO’s definition of “Large Load” into its TO Tariff

points.point: A new appendix holds the large load interconnection procedures.
points.quote: SCE proposes to create a new Appendix titled the Large Load Interconnection Procedures (“LLIP”) to augment existing TO Tariff interconnection and cost responsibility sections

points.point: A request needs a $250,000 study deposit and a readiness deposit of twice that.
points.quote: an Interconnection Study Deposit of $250,000, a Commercial Readiness Deposit equal to two times the study deposit

points.point: The same transmission rules apply to SCE's own retail large load customers.
points.quote: SCE’s LLIP thus applies the same transmission-related requirements to SCE’s own Large Load retail transmission customers as it does to Eligible Customers seeking to interconnect on behalf of Large Loads

points.point: A 15-year minimum revenue obligation backed by five years of security protects against stranded network upgrade costs.
points.quote: a 15-year minimum transmission revenue obligation backed by 5 years of security

points.point: Early termination after service starts costs the customer all remaining required security.
points.quote: early termination triggers an Exit Fee equal to all remaining required security, including the MARO security, due within 30 Business Days

points.point: Curtailment terms for the interim service sit in an appendix to the security and reliability agreement.
points.quote: the conditions and limitations applicable to FILI service, including curtailments, are specified in Appendix E to the TSRA

points.point: SCE says the California owners should not be expected to file uniform tariffs.
points.quote: SCE believes uniformity in the PTOs’ tariffs should not be expected

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-10 show cause order for SCE's own transmission owner tariff. SCE says it covers the application, cost shifting and flexible service items and expects other owners' tariffs to differ.

figures.label: Security agreement term
figures.quote: The TSRA has a term of 15 years from its effective date
